full_judgment: 5. This Court appreciates that the purpose and scheme of the Act is fundamentally to tax every stage at which value is found to be added. Conversely, any attempt at taxation at any stage when such value addition has not taken place shall be deemed to be one not contemplated in the law and thereby, unlawful and without jurisdiction. It is against the above factual and legal backdrop that the petitioner is now faced with the Respondents demand to secure registration under section 15 of the Act of the various "sale centres" that the petitioner has been found to be operating in Dhaka, the presumption being that by the very nature of the business transacted through any "sale centre" the petitioner exposes itself to the additional liability for payment of VAT over and above that which may have been levied and paid at the very initial stages of the supply process as described above. The attribution to the petitioner's activities from these "sale/distribution centres" is one of acting for profit, thereby, leading to its registered status as supplier/manufacturer to be converted at this stage to that of ব্যবসায়ী or trader. The Affidavit in Opposition on behalf of the Respondent No. 2 Commissioner of Customs, Exercise and VAT, in dwelling on this aspect justifies the categorization of the petitioner as a trader in that its activities through the "sale/distribution centres" in Dhaka are found to be akin to that of a distributor engaged in the sale of goods from such "centres". The bottom line, the Respondent No. 2 asserts is that any such "centre" is in reality a trading organization and that the very act of supplying goods to the distributors from these "centres" has the manufacturer assuming the role of a trader. Such categorization it appears arises from a deep-seated concern of the government to rein in various activities that may qualify as ব্যবসা or trade for value with the objective the widening the VAT tax liability bracket.
